problemStatement.formal: \text{For a connected hypergraph } H \text{ where every vertex has even degree, there exists an Eulerian circuit traversing every hyperedge exactly once.}
problemStatement.plain: Complete the work-in-progress Lean proof extending the classical Konigsberg bridge result to hypergraphs, where edges may connect more than two vertices, and to the related infinite-graph setting.
whyMatters: Hypergraph Euler paths generalize the classical bridge-crossing theorem to richer combinatorial structures.
Completing this proof would close a work-in-progress gap in the gallery's combinatorics coverage.

proven: Classical Eulerian circuits in finite graphs are known from the degree condition.
The parent konigsberg-oq-03 gallery entry contains partial work.
open: Complete the Lean 4 proof for hypergraph Eulerian paths.

insights: **True placeholders are dishonest formalisation**: KonigsbergOQ03.lean has 0 sorries and 0 axioms but until 2026-06-03 had 3 (later 2) :=True propositions, which makes its 0-sorry count misleading. Per CLAUDE.md Aristotle rule #3 (No placeholder True theorems), the same principle applies broadly — True propositions are gaps masquerading as completeness. As of S4 ACT, all 3 are discharged.

**r=2 hypergraph IS a SimpleGraph** — the natural reduction is to convert RUniformHypergraph V 2 to SimpleGraph V via edges (each Finset V of size 2 becomes an unordered pair), then use Mathlib SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian. This is the cleanest small-scope target (~30 LOC), shipped in S3 ACT.
**r≥3 hypergraph Euler tours are NP-complete** (Lonc-Naroski 2010) — there is no simple degree condition characterising existence. The file docstring acknowledges this but offers no path forward.

**The sibling slug konigsberg-oq-03-oq-02 already paid the infinite-walk infrastructure cost**: KonigsbergOQ03OQ02.lean ships InfiniteWalk (ℕ-indexed) + IsEulerWalk + BiInfiniteWalk + IsBiInfiniteEulerWalk + HasOneWayInfiniteEulerPath in ~85 LOC. The S2 SURVEY's projection of 200-400 LOC new infrastructure was conservative because this sibling was not visible to the parent stub maintainers. S4 ACT ports that infrastructure to the parent file.

**Sibling-parent duplication can be collapsed in a follow-up DRY pass** (~100 LOC reduction): KonigsbergOQ03OQ02.lean currently redeclares InfiniteGraph + InfiniteWalk + IsEulerWalk + BiInfiniteWalk for self-containment (with a stale justification: the parent's dependency on the build-broken Konigsberg.lean was removed in S3 ACT). A future refactor under the sibling slug konigsberg-oq-03-oq-02 should import the parent and drop the duplicates. Pure refactor, no new math.

**ℕ-indexed-function representation beats Stream' for infinite walks**: avoids coinductive complexity while remaining mathematically equivalent (interconvertible without extra hypotheses). The sibling file's docstring explicitly chose this; S4 ACT inherits the choice.

Only the edge-INJECTIVITY half of IsEulerWalk is needed for finite-edge impossibility — the covers half is irrelevant, so the core lemma lives at InfiniteWalk level, strictly stronger than the Euler-path corollaries.

Directed arcs (V x V) beat Sym2 for the finiteness hypothesis: the step map lands in arcSet definitionally (w.step_adj n IS the membership proof), avoiding Sym2 quotient plumbing; arc-set finiteness is equivalent to undirected-edge finiteness (2-to-1).

For the ZZ-indexed BiInfiniteWalk the injectivity extraction inverts: IsBiInfiniteEulerWalk states m ≠ n -> ¬sameEdge, so injectivity of the step map comes by_contra on the index equality rather than directly.
Identity walks make the ray/line Euler witnesses nearly free: step_adj is Or.inl rfl, coverage witness is the vertex itself, and sameEdge injectivity reduces to linear arithmetic omega closes.

Positive witnesses x impossibility theorems compose: rayGraph has an Euler path, finite-arc graphs cannot, so rayGraph has infinitely many arcs — non-degeneracy of the S11 results demonstrated inside the file.

Ray (one-ended) vs line (two-ended) is the right witness pair: it sets up the S13 incomparability program (ray: one-way yes / bi-infinite conjecturally no; line: bi-infinite yes / one-way conjecturally no).
